claims.text: A quality improvement study at Houston Methodist Hospital examined inpatient encounters discharged between August 1st, 2023 and February 28th, 2024.
claims.quote: This quality improvement study included inpatient encounters at Houston Methodist Hospital with discharge dates between August 1, 2023, and February 28, 2024.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: A day before discharge, case managers placed far more of their estimates within one day of the real date than the AI tool did.
claims.quote: At 24 hours, 79.5% of case manager estimations fell within 1 day vs 37.9% for AI estimations
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: Closer to discharge the case managers beat the tool on mean absolute error at both the 48 hour and the 24 hour mark.
claims.quote: Nearer to discharge, case managers vs AI were more accurate (48 hours: MAE, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.26-1.32] vs 1.59 [95% CI 1.57-1.61] days; 24 hours: MAE, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-1.01] vs 1.93 [95% CI, 1.91-1.95] days) (both P < .001).
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open
claims.note: The second bracket really does print 95% CI without the comma the other three carry. Reproduced as printed. Do not tidy it.

claims.text: At admission the two methods sat close together on error, and the case managers still hit the exact date and landed within one day more often than the tool.
claims.quote: At admission, accuracy was similar between methods (MAE, 4.20 [95% CI, 4.08-4.31] vs 4.27 [4.15-4.38] days; P = .001), although case managers matched the exact date more often (23.6% vs 15.3%) and fell within 1 day more often (46.3% vs 40.8%).
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open
claims.note: In every pair the FIRST figure is the case managers and the second is the AI. A slide that reverses them reverses the story.

claims.text: The dates came from a commercial clinician assisted tool wired into the electronic health record.
claims.quote: Artificial intelligence–estimated discharge dates were generated by a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the EHR.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open
claims.note: The quote carries an en dash in 'intelligence-estimated'. It is verbatim and stays inside the quote. Nothing outside a quote may reproduce it.

claims.text: The study found the AI estimate matched usual care at admission and lost to case managers as discharge approached, which is when an accurate date is most useful for managing beds.
claims.quote: This quality improvement study found that AI-estimated discharge was comparable to usual care at admission but outperformed by case managers as discharge approached (when accurate estimations are most actionable for bed management).
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: The authors warn that the strong correlation at admission can't be read as evidence the tool captured what clinicians know across the stay.
claims.quote: The strong admission correlation did not persist nearer discharge and should not be interpreted as evidence that the tool captured the same information clinicians use throughout the stay.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: The authors flag a limitation on their own side of the comparison. Case manager estimates were visible to care teams and may be partly self fulfilling, while the AI estimates sat in the record without being switched on automatically.
claims.quote: Case manager estimates were part of usual care and visible to care teams, so they may be partly self-fulfilling and, thus, advantaged nearer discharge; AI estimations were accessible in the EHR but not enabled automatically.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open
claims.note: The honest caveat. A deck that runs the human win without it is overclaiming.

claims.text: The authors call for prospective outcome based evaluation before anyone decides the tool's extra accuracy in some subgroups is worth what it takes to run it.
claims.quote: Whether the AI's incremental accuracy in selected subgroups justifies the complexity of implementation warrants prospective, outcome-based evaluation.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open
claims.note: The page says complexity, not cost.

claims.text: The number of encounters compared is reported separately at each of the three time points.
claims.quote: admission, n = 21 710; 48 hours, n = 9236; 24 hours, n = 12 172
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open
claims.note: Counts print with a thin space inside the thousands. No ranking or subtraction across these three may be asserted.

claims.text: The comparison carries no patient demographics at all, which the authors state outright as a limitation.
claims.quote: No baseline patient demographic data were available.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: The study reports itself against the SQUIRE reporting guideline, the standard for quality improvement work.
claims.quote: The study followed the SQUIRE reporting guideline.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: Three named clinicians wrote the study.
claims.quote: Havish S Kantheti, MD, Connor Dolan, BS, Jordan Dale, MD
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: The study appeared in JAMA Network Open on September 3rd, 2026.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients, JAMA Network Open

claims.text: ERCOT told the market it will hold a workshop on October 6th, 2026 covering how large load curtailment under Senate Bill 6 is meant to work.
claims.quote: On October 6, 2026 ERCOT will host a workshop to present the deployment mechanics, registration process, and draft revision requests for Large Load curtailment under Senate Bill 6 (SB6).

claims.text: Senate Bill 6 put three large load provisions into PURA, and one of them lets ERCOT order large loads whose backup generation covers a stated share of their own demand to cut what they draw from the grid during emergency conditions.
claims.quote: SB6 established several provisions in PURA related to Large Loads, including an authorization for the PUC to require Large Loads that co-locate with existing Generation Resources to reduce consumption during certain events (section 39.169); an authorization for ERCOT to require Large Loads with backup generation serving at least 50% of their load to curtail their grid consumption when necessary to mitigate actual or potential EEA conditions (section 37.0561(e)); and a requirement for the PUC to establish a large load demand management service (section 39.170).
claims.note: The 50% threshold stays inside the quote. Copy may not restate it, round it or call it 'half'.

claims.text: The council's own agenda states what the September 8th public hearing was on, and the part of the city charter a citizen petition brought it under.
claims.quote: Public Hearing - City Secretary: Conduct a public hearing in accordance with Chapter 1, Article IV, Section 1 of the City of Lubbock Charter, regarding an "18-month moratorium on high-water-use and high-energy-use data centers in the City of Lubbock, Lubbock County, Texas."
claims.source_title: City of Lubbock, Regular City Council Meeting agenda, September 8th, 2026
claims.note: Verified by exact string match against the text of the agenda PDF, extracted with pypdf in this run, alongside an altered control that correctly failed to match. The fact-checker could not read this document at all and rejected it as UNREADABLE rather than as false.

claims.text: The agenda states what the resolution beside the hearing would do, and what it waits on.
claims.quote: Resolution - City Council: Consider a resolution expressing the City Council's desire that large-scale data centers not be developed within the municipal limits of the City of Lubbock, until the City Council has adopted regulations protecting public resources and the public health and safety.
claims.source_title: City of Lubbock, Regular City Council Meeting agenda, September 8th, 2026
claims.note: Same verification as c17. A resolution states a desire and an ordinance states a rule, and this quote is what keeps the two apart.

rejected.finding: The JAMA Network Open paper names no vendor or product anywhere
rejected.reason: An absence this retrieval path cannot prove. What is verified and carries the same editorial weight is c5, where the paper describes the tool only as a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the EHR. Say that instead of saying no vendor is named.

rejected.finding: The authors' institutional affiliations as printed lines
rejected.reason: Substantively confirmed on two fetches and rejected on string integrity. The affiliation lines print with superscript markers, so a leading digit could be a rendering artifact rather than a printed character, and a quote nobody can find by searching the page is not a quote. c13 carries the names and c1 carries the hospital.

rejected.finding: Battalion Oil's equity investment in Collide, September 8th, 2026
rejected.reason: A corporate release describing a plan with a day 90 milestone and no measured result. Nothing has been deployed and the financial terms are undisclosed, so there is no decision here the record could carry yet.

rejected.finding: PUCT Project 58555, the ERCOT ancillary and reliability services cost allocation study, workshop September 22nd
rejected.reason: Read in full, including the workshop agenda memo filed September 8th. Its three alternative cost allocation methods and its questions for comment mention no large load, no data center and no artificial intelligence anywhere. It is a grid cost allocation proceeding and it is not this record's subject.

rejected.reason: No docket number, division or assigned judge was obtained, and a CourtListener RECAP search of the Southern District of Texas returned nothing, so the filing could not be confirmed against a primary court record.
